title: Quality check, evidence and handover for specialty appliance cleaning
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: NSW Government, Electricians (last updated 1 December 2025).
audience: Workers and supervisors who finish appliance cleaning jobs, check the result and hand over the appliance and the record to the site
learningOutcomes: Inspect a cleaned appliance against the agreed standard and the safety checks
Restore the appliance to its pre-job arrangement, including guards, covers, trays and labels
Record photographs, product use, exclusions and referrals accurately
Write a handover statement that is accurate, within scope and free of safety or warranty promises

instruction.heading: What the finished check must confirm
instruction.body: A finished appliance clean is checked by eye and by hand before it is handed over. The eye check confirms that the surfaces are clean and dry, that there are no streaks, residue, scratches or moisture at seams, that the labels and data plate are readable, and that the door seal sits correctly and has no visible tear. The hand check confirms that the control panel is dry at its edges, that trays and bins are seated and not loose, and that covers and guards are fitted correctly. Check that no water has entered a vent, socket, switch or motor housing, and that no tool or cloth has been left in or near the machine. Check that every part you were asked to clean is done, and that every part you excluded is recorded as excluded. The finish check is about the agreed standard. It does not test whether the appliance works, and it does not confirm that the appliance is safe to use.

instruction.heading: Restore the machine and leave it as the site expects
instruction.body: Put back everything you removed, including trays, racks, drip trays, bin liners and guards, and return them to their correct positions. Confirm that the isolation applied under “Making a machine safe before cleaning: isolation, stored energy and moving parts” is removed only by the person who applied it, and that the removal is recorded. Do not switch the machine on to test it unless the site procedure and the manufacturer's instructions allow it, and the site contact has agreed, because switching on is not part of the cleaning service. Tell the site contact in plain words what state the machine is in, and what they should check before they use it. If the machine must remain off, say so and record it. Leave the work area clean and dry, and remove all waste, cloths and product containers from the area. A tidy site is part of the job and protects the next user.

instruction.heading: Evidence and handover statement
instruction.body: Every job needs an evidence record that someone else could read and understand without you. Record each appliance by make, model, serial number and location. Record the before and after photographs with the data plate in shot where the business requires it. Record the products used, from the approved list, with the dilution and the surface. Record the parts excluded and the reason, such as gas components, refrigerant circuits, internal water parts, or internal electrical parts. Record every defect, leak, fault code or damage found, and the referral made and to whom. The handover statement should say what was cleaned, to what standard, what was excluded and why, what was referred, and what the site must arrange next. It must not say that the machine is safe, that it works, or that it complies with any regulation. If the record shows a fault, the handover says so plainly. The defect reporting route and the evidence needed are set by the business's quality record.

procedure: Walk around the appliance and check the surfaces for streaks, residue, scratches and moisture at seams, using the approved standard.
Check the control panel, sockets, vents and seals by hand and by eye for water, product and damage.
Refit all trays, racks, drip trays, bins, covers and guards in their correct positions, and confirm they are seated.
Confirm that the isolation was removed by the person who applied it, and record the removal time.
Check that no cloth, tool or container is left in or near the machine, and that the area is clean, dry and free of waste.
Take the after photographs of the appliance, with the data plate in shot where the business requires it.
Write the handover statement with what was cleaned, the standard reached, the exclusions and the referrals.
Hand over to the site contact in person, explain the state of the machine, and record the name and time of the handover.

workedExamples.situation: You finish cleaning a commercial dishwasher's fascia and the control panel. A small wet line is visible at the seam where the control panel meets the fascia. The booking says the job is complete when the machine is clean.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the job complete, and what goes in the handover?
workedExamples.reasoning: The job is not complete to the standard until the wet line is dried and checked. Dry the seam with a dry cloth, wipe away any residue, and check again. If the line remains, record it with a photograph, because it may be a pre-existing leak or a seal fault, and refer it. The handover must say what was cleaned, that a moisture line was found at the seam and what was done, and that the seam needs a check by the owner's service provider. Do not say the machine is watertight.

workedExamples.situation: You finish an external clean of a commercial oven. The booking was to clean the exterior and the racks. The site contact asks you to confirm in the handover that the oven is ready to use for service tonight.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you write in the handover?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not confirm that the oven is ready for service, because the clean does not test the oven. Write what was cleaned, the racks and exterior, that the internal and gas parts were not part of the job, and that the oven has not been operated or tested by you. Recommend that the site arranges any test under its own procedure and by its own qualified provider. Record the statement and the time.

equipmentAndPpe: Clean, dry microfibre cloths for the final wipe
Camera or device for before and after photographs
Handover template or checklist from the business quality record
Gloves and eye protection as set by the business, removed safely before handover

commonErrors.error: Writing that the machine is safe or working in the handover because it looks clean.
commonErrors.prevention: State what was cleaned and what was excluded. Do not state safety, function or compliance outcomes.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a guard, tray or cover off after the clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the restore step as a checklist, and confirm each item is back in position before handover.

commonErrors.error: Forgetting to record excluded parts and referrals, so the business cannot show what was and was not done.
commonErrors.prevention: Record every excluded part and every referral in the job record before you leave the site.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A visual clean does not confirm the safety, function or compliance of an appliance. Any statement that goes beyond the cleaning standard is a claim the worker cannot support.

This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or authority to inspect, test or certify any appliance, gas installation, electrical installation or refrigeration system. As one example, NSW requires a licence before any electrical wiring work.
The clean handover must not imply that completing this course qualifies the worker to certify any regulated work.

qualityStandard: The surfaces, seams, labels and seals are checked by eye and by hand and meet the agreed standard
All parts are restored, the isolation is removed by the person who applied it, and the site is left clean and dry
The handover statement states what was cleaned, what was excluded and what was referred, with no safety or warranty claim
documentationEvidence: Before and after photographs of each appliance, with the data plate in shot where required
The products used, from the approved list, with dilution and surface, and the exclusions and reasons
The handover statement, the name of the site contact and the time of handover
summary: Check surfaces, seams and seals by eye and hand, and restore all trays, guards and covers.
Remove isolation only by the person who applied it, and do not switch on the machine without agreement.
The handover states what was cleaned, what was excluded and what was referred, and it makes no safety or working claim.

knowledgeChecks.question: At the end of an appliance clean, what does the finish check confirm?
options: That the appliance is safe to use, so the customer can switch it on straight away after the clean
That the agreed cleaning standard has been met, including surfaces, seams, seals and restoration of parts
That the appliance passes a manufacturer inspection, which covers every part and every electrical test
That the appliance works correctly, including all of its electrical and gas functions after the clean

knowledgeChecks.question: A wet line is found at a control panel seam after cleaning. What is the correct action?
options: Ignore it because the job is finished and the customer has already paid
Write that the machine is watertight, since the seam was cleaned thoroughly today
Dry and recheck, and if the line remains, photograph, record and refer it
Seal the seam with a sealant from your van, so the customer does not see the line

knowledgeChecks.question: Who should remove an isolation from a machine at the end of the job?
options: The site contact, without telling the worker who applied the isolation first
Any customer who asks for the machine to be turned on, once the clean is done
The first person to enter the room after the job has finished for the day
The person who applied the isolation, after checking the machine is clear

knowledgeChecks.question: Which handover statement is appropriate?
options: The external surfaces and racks were cleaned to the agreed standard, and gas and internal parts were excluded and referred
The oven is ready for service tonight and fully compliant with every standard that applies to commercial kitchens
The fryer has been tested and is safe for use, with its thermostat and oil level checked by the cleaner
The refrigeration circuit has been checked and is leak free, so the unit can run at full capacity for the night

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must excluded parts be recorded in the job record?
options: So the customer can be charged for the excluded parts later, once the work is finished
So the business can show what was and was not done, and who was told about the referrals
So the worker can avoid writing the photographs and the short notes at the end of the job
So the parts can be cleaned by the next worker without any authority, once the record is closed
